language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi, my name is Kamoku. This is Mrs. Gren’s tiki hut.
I often stop by the Tiki hut after school to visit with Mrs. Gren. She likes to make my favourite drink, a coco-choco served in a coconut shell. It’s yummy!

Yesterday, during my visit, Mrs. Gren told me that all living things go through 7 life processes. Mrs. Gren gave me a tip. She told me to use the letters in her name to remember the name of each process.
Notice how the letters on the coco-choco drinks spell Mrs. Gren?
Learn about each of the 7 life processes!
Movement. Animals move around to find shelter, escape from predators and dangers. Find food or find a mate!
Reproduction. Animals have babies.
Sensitivity. Animals use their senses to find food, find their way around, or escape danger.
Growth. All living things grow!
Respiration. This occurs when glucose, a type of sugar that you get from food, reacts with oxygen to produce energy.
Excretion. Gets rid of carbon dioxide, water, and other harmful substances from the body.
Nutrition. Animals must eat, in order to have energy.

All animals must eat to get nutrients that helps them survive. Some animals get their nutrients from plants only, they are called herbivores.
Some animals get their nutrients by eating other animals, they are called carnivores. Some animals get their nutrients from both plants and animals; they are called omnivores.
Can you look at the pictures of animals and help me figure out if they are herbivores, carnivores or omnivores?

There are a lot of things that all animals do to make sure they stay alive and have babies. Scientists call these, "life processes". Scientists like to make up difficult words for normal things. Can you guess which life process belongs to which description?
